    Prediction: Rocket Lab Will Triple Its Revenue by 2028. Here’s What That Would Mean for the Stock.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Plenty of companies are growing incredibly well right now, including several from the artificial intelligence business.
    • Except for orbital launch and satellite tech specialist Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%), it isn't.
    • Rocket Lab offers satellite launch solutions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Brumley – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Rocket Lab ›.

    Plenty of companies are growing incredibly well right now, including several from the artificial intelligence business. A firm that's set to triple its top line over the course of the next couple of years, though? That seems outrageous.

    Except for orbital launch and satellite tech specialist Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%), it isn't. This future business is already lined up. These paying customers are just waiting for one pivotal milestone that's likely to materialize sometime next year. Then the floodgates open.

    Rocket Lab offers satellite launch solutions. Its relatively small Electron rocket design has now been launched 100 times, putting 273 satellites into low earth orbit.

    The organization also provides a range of satellite components and construction services, which accounts for more than half of last quarter's revenue of $268 million. Rocket Lab expects to do around $980 billion in business in fiscal 2026, well up from last year's $602 billion.

    According to recent reports, this is just a taste of what's to come, though. As the company confirmed with its third-quarter report posted earlier this month, Rocket Lab's backlog grew 52% from Q2's $2.36 billion to an incredible $3.6 billion. The organization just needs more capacity, but that's coming. Rocket Lab can now manufacture an Electron rocket every eight days.

    Then there's the proverbial 800-pound gorilla in the room. That's the firm's larger Neutron rocket, which has seen its inaugural flight pushed back several times, with the first flight now expected sometime in 2027.

    Industry observers note that despite the delays so far, once Neutron is flying, everything takes a turn for the better. As CFO Adam Spice commented during the third-quarter's earnings conference call, adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) "will turn positive within six months of that first successful test flight," with cash flow likely to turn positive shortly after that.

    Neutron isn't the significant profit center in and of itself, to be clear. It's just a means to an end. Being able to put larger, heavier satellites into orbit also opens up its satellite tech business. Of its newly introduced backlog of $3.6 billion, $1.7 billion of it reflects space systems rather than launch services, up 194% year over year.

    According to recent reports, to this end, while analysts aren't yet looking for Rocket Lab's revenue to triple between now and 2028, with recent failures of similar rockets like ULA's Vulcan and one earlier in the year from Blue Origin, Rocket Lab is quickly becoming a preferred launch option. It may well exceed 2028's expectations.

    Recent findings suggest that as for the impact on the stock, it's not a complicated prediction to make. If the company's top line comes anywhere close to tripling by 2028, the bullish argument firms up enormously.

    Recent findings suggest that while it may not triple in value in step with revenue, $3 billion in sales could turn this high-growth $34 billion outfit into a $60 billion outfit with relative ease. And given that the firm isn't likely to raise money by issuing more stock anytime soon, that translates into a near-doubling of the stock's price.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that you're getting some help in the meantime, by the way. The analyst community overwhelmingly considers RKLB stock a strong buy right now, with a 12-month consensus price target of $93.30 already more than 80% above the ticker's current price.

    Prediction: Nvidia Stock Will Do This in the 6 Months After a Fresh CEO Takes Over, According to History

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (903 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) is navigating one of the most consequential leadership transitions in recent Silicon Valley history.
    • Recent findings suggest that colette Kress, Nvidia's former chief financial officer, is now serving as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.
    • History offers some clues about how technology stocks behave following major CEO transitions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:42PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) is navigating one of the most consequential leadership transitions in recent Silicon Valley history. Following founder Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation amid a controversy involving alleged connections to Chinese intelligence, investors are growing increasingly concerned about the firm's future. This uncertainty is weighing heavily on Nvidia stock, even as its underlying business continues to deliver extraordinary financial results.

    Recent findings suggest that colette Kress, Nvidia's former chief financial officer, is now serving as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. According to reports, the company is considering external candidates, including Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas.

    History offers some clues about how technology stocks behave following major CEO transitions. However, Nvidia's circumstances are quite different from those of its peers, making the firm's financial outlook particularly crucial right now.

    Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) represents a successful example of a technology leadership transition. Satya Nadella became CEO on Feb. 4, 2014, replacing Steve Ballmer after Microsoft conducted a formal succession search. Nadella had previously led Microsoft's cloud and enterprise businesses, giving him extensive knowledge of the company's operations.

    Industry observers note that microsoft stock advanced roughly 19% during Nadella's first six months as CEO. Of course, over the long term, he helped transform the Windows developer into a cloud computing powerhouse.

    Industry observers note that alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%) offers another example. Sundar Pichai became CEO of Alphabet on Dec. 3, 2019, succeeding co-founder Larry Page. However, Pichai had already served as Google's CEO since 2015, making the transition more of a consolidation of leadership responsibilities than an unexpected management overhaul.

    According to recent reports, alphabet stock was higher roughly six months later, despite experiencing a meaningful drawdown during the short-lived COVID-19 market crash. Moreover, Page and his co-founder Sergey Brin remained involved as shareholders and directors, providing continuity that Nvidia currently lacks.

    In a recent development, amazon (AMZN -4.10%) experienced a different outcome when Andy Jassy succeeded Jeff Bezos on July 5, 2021. Jassy was another internal executive who had previously built and led Amazon Web Services (AWS). Although Bezos relinquished the CEO position, he remains executive chairman, preserving his influence over the tech giant's long-term strategy.

    In a recent development, amazon shares declined approximately 6% during Jassy's first six months as CEO. At the time, investors were assessing the impacts of slowing pandemic-era growth and rising operating expenses on Amazon's e-commerce marketplace.

    In a recent development, the three examples above show that CEO succession can bring different short-term outcomes. However, they also share an important characteristic: Each of these companies promoted an experienced internal executive through an orderly transition, unlike Nvidia's abrupt leadership disruption.

    Nvidia's situation is unusual because Huang wasn't just another corporate executive. He co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and spent more than three decades directing the manufacturer's evolution from a graphics chip manufacturer into the world's leading supplier of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. His influence extended across engineering, product development, corporate culture, and customer relationships.

    As a result of his departure, investors are increasingly questioning whether Nvidia can maintain its technological edge without the executive who helped establish it. The uncertainty is compounded by growing competition from custom AI accelerators developed by Alphabet, Amazon, and other hyperscalers. Nvidia's next CEO needs to prove they can preserve the tech giant's innovation-driven culture while navigating complicated supply chains and regulatory relationships.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that despite the unusual circumstances, Nvidia's financial outlook provides a compelling reason to anticipate a meaningful recovery. During its fiscal third-quarter earnings call, management increased its fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast to 75%, up from its previous outlook of 70%. This suggests demand for Nvidia's accelerated computing platforms remains strong despite Huang's departure.

    Recent findings suggest that furthermore, Nvidia expects to generate $130 billion in revenue during the fourth quarter -- representing 91% growth year over year. The company is also forecasting gross margins of between 72% and 73% in fiscal 2028, suggesting that accelerating sales growth will translate into additional profits.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia's share repurchase program provides another subtle catalyst for the stock. In September, the board increased the company's existing authorization by $150 billion, leaving approximately $227.3 billion available at the end of the third quarter. Management intends to execute the remaining authorization by the end of fiscal 2028.

    By reducing the number of outstanding shares, stock buybacks can increase earnings per share (EPS) even if net income is unchanged. Combined with Nvidia's revenue growth and profit margins, upcoming share repurchases should fuel substantial EPS expansion over the coming year.

    In a recent development, my prediction is that Nvidia stock will trade higher six months after its upcoming CEO assumes the role. The appointment itself should remove the primary source of uncertainty around the organization, allowing investors to concentrate once again on revenue growth, earnings power, and competitive advantages.

    Here's How Much Nvidia Stock Is Worth Without Jensen Huang, According to Dan Ives

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (942 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) has experienced a stunning reversal following founder Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation amid controversy surrounding alleged connections to Chinese intelligence.
    • Sources indicate that the magnitude of the decline is anything but trivial.
    • Industry observers note that nevertheless, Wall Street analyst Dan Ives thinks investors are overlooking Nvidia's underlying earnings power.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:10PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) has experienced a stunning reversal following founder Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation amid controversy surrounding alleged connections to Chinese intelligence. Investors are increasingly questioning whether the semiconductor behemoth can maintain its technological edge without the executive who spent more than three decades building the organization. Those concerns have contributed to a dramatic sell-off, even as Nvidia continues reporting ridiculously good financial results.

    Sources indicate that the magnitude of the decline is anything but trivial. Nvidia stock reached a record closing price of around $239 in early October but has fallen to roughly $136 as of Nov. 20. That represents a decline of roughly 43%, wiping out more than $2.5 trillion in market capitalization and pushing Nvidia from the world's most valuable public company to fourth place.

    NVDA Market Cap data by YCharts.

    Industry observers note that nevertheless, Wall Street analyst Dan Ives thinks investors are overlooking Nvidia's underlying earnings power. Although he acknowledges that Huang's departure changes the tech giant's investment thesis, his revised price target suggests meaningful upside remains.

    It has been revealed that ives has been particularly vocal about the consequences of Huang's resignation. During a recent interview, he estimated that Huang contributed $1 trillion to Nvidia's valuation. In a separate appearance, Ives described Huang as the company's "heart and lungs," emphasizing his influence over Nvidia's technological roadmap and competitive position.

    Sources indicate that ives says Nvidia stock is worth $225 without Huang and $300 with him as CEO. These figures provide an interesting way to quantify the so-called Jensen premium. The difference between Ives' two valuations is $75 per share, representing a 25% reduction from his original $300 target.

    The implied difference in market capitalization is actually considerably larger than the $1 trillion Ives alluded to. With approximately 24.2 billion shares outstanding, a $75 difference translates into roughly $1.8 trillion in equity value. At Ives' respective price targets, Nvidia would command a market capitalization of approximately $7.3 trillion with Huang and $5.4 trillion without him.

    The difference in valuation illustrates the enormous importance Wall Street places on Nvidia's founder and why investors have reacted so negatively to his departure.

    Recent findings suggest that dan Ives. Image source: Getty Images.

    Huang's value extends beyond his responsibilities as CEO. Since co-founding Nvidia in 1993, he has overseen the company's transformation from a graphics processing company into the dominant supplier of accelerated computing infrastructure. His investments in GPUs, CUDA software, and AI computing helped position Nvidia at the center of the technology industry's most key transformation since the birth of the internet.

    Perhaps Huang's greatest contribution has been leading Nvidia's culture of innovation. Huang consistently anticipated computing trends years before they became commercially relevant. This enabled Nvidia to develop new chip architectures and software ecosystems that competitors have struggled to replicate. This foresight helps establish durable competitive advantages and contributes to the organization's pricing power.

    Huang also cultivated relationships with other technology executives, hyperscalers, governments, and AI labs. These supply chain connections have become crucial as Nvidia participates in data center build-outs that require complex financing arrangements and long-term strategic commitments.

    With all of that noted, Nvidia's competitive advantages are not going to disappear just because Huang stepped away. The company's hardware and software ecosystem, engineering workforce, customer relationships, and product roadmap remain intact.

    In a recent development, moreover, Ives acknowledges that Nvidia has a lead of two to three years over its competitors in AI chip technology. Although Huang's departure could narrow that advantage over time, the company's existing leadership provides a robust foundation for future growth.

    Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

    It has been revealed that despite reducing his Nvidia price target from $300 to $225, Ives maintains a bullish outlook on the company. At approximately $136 per share, his revised target implies roughly 65% upside, while his original $300 estimate implies 121% potential appreciation.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that importantly, Ives' optimism centers on the insatiable demand for AI computing infrastructure and Nvidia's technological advantages. Following the firm's earnings report on Nov. 17, Ives wrote that the results answered a critical question: "Demand did not leave with him.".

    Sources indicate that the financial evidence supports that assessment. Nvidia generated $115.8 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, representing 103% growth year over year, while data center revenue surged 110% to $107.6 billion. The firm also reported a gross margin of 74.8%, demonstrating that its pricing power remains strong.

    According to recent reports, furthermore, Nvidia forecast $130 billion in revenue for the fourth quarter and raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75%. This forecast suggests the manufacturer is poised for further expansion despite the leadership transition.

    The central takeaway from Ives' analysis is that Nvidia doesn't necessarily need Huang to remain an attractive investment. Although his departure has reduced -- for now -- the premium investors are willing to pay, his price target still suggests considerable appreciation over the coming year. For investors who can stomach short-term volatility, Nvidia's recent sell-off could represent an opportunity to buy the dip in the most dominant AI infrastructure business at a significantly discounted valuation.

    Top Wall Street analysts are upbeat about the prospects for these 3 stocks

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%.
    • In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

    In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Neocloud company CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

    In a recent development, recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

    It has been revealed that chatterjee said CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

    Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

    In a recent development, "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," said Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

    Chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

    Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

    Industry observers note that after a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

    Industry observers note that over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security manufacturer, Powell stated. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

    Meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell noted.

    BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

    Industry observers note that powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

    In a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he said.

    Sources indicate that devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

    Sources indicate that additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

    Overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the tech giant if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he said. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

    Recent findings suggest that "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," mentioned Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

    It has been revealed that devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Latest Update: Bristol Myers Squibb's Growth Portfolio Just Hit $7.7 Billion. Is This Cheap Pharma Stock a No-Brainer Buy?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (707 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:15PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Bristol Myers Squibb ›.
    • Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY +0.79%) is a large, well-respected pharmaceutical organization.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bristol Myers Squibb ›.

    Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY +0.79%) is a large, well-respected pharmaceutical organization. It traces its history back to the mid-1800s. Right now, the company's portfolio of newer drugs, which it calls its "growth portfolio", just generated nearly $7.7 billion in revenue in a single quarter. That's a 12% increase over the same quarter in 2025. But is the stock worth buying? The risk/reward balance looks tilted toward reward for all but the most conservative investors. Here's why.

    Industry observers note that the success Bristol Myers Squibb is having with its growth portfolio clearly indicates that this pharmaceutical giant hasn't lost its mojo. But investors are still downbeat on the stock (more on this below). So the dividend yield is a lofty 4.3%. The S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%) yields roughly 1.1%, the average healthcare stock yields 1.3%, and the average drug stock yields 1.3%. That above-market and industry yield will likely be very enticing to long-term dividend investors. Meanwhile, the roughly 55% dividend payout ratio leaves ample room for adversity and should mollify all but the most conservative income lovers.

    Notably, the dividend has been increased regularly, though not annually, for over three decades. There have been no dividend cuts along the way despite the organization working through some difficult periods during that span. That shows the board of directors is strongly committed to returning value to shareholders through a reliable, slowly growing dividend. Adding to the allure is the fact that the stock's 13x price-to-earnings ratio is notably below the pharma industry average of roughly 28x. The high yield and relatively low P/E ratio will likely be of interest to value investors.

    Recent findings suggest that growth investors will appreciate the above-highlighted success of the company's growth portfolio. That portfolio is a collection of over a dozen newly introduced drugs that, as of the third quarter, account for nearly 60% of the company's drug revenues. That's good news and bad news, however, and it highlights the risk that investors face if they decide to buy Bristol Myers Squibb.

    The healthcare giant's legacy portfolio still accounts for around 40% of revenues, or roughly $5.4 billion. And one drug, Eliquis, is responsible for nearly $4.7 billion of that total. Eliquis is set to see generic competition as soon as 2028. When that happens, the revenue this drug produces will likely start to fall, and perhaps sharply. That is why investors remain downbeat on Bristol Myers Squibb's stock despite the success of its growth portfolio.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that it is reasonable that extremely conservative investors might want to stay on the sidelines until after Eliquis' patent expires. However, it is important to remember that patent expirations are just a normal part of the pharmaceutical business. And given the success of the growth portfolio, Bristol Myers Squibb continues to execute well in fresh drug development. There's just a mismatch between when patents expire, which happens on a set schedule, and its development efforts, which do not happen on a set schedule.

    According to recent reports, in order to buy Bristol Myers Squibb, you need to believe it will get through this period. History suggests it will, and that's backed up by the success of the growth portfolio.

    In a recent development, if you can't handle the uncertainty around the patent expiration of Eliquis, you shouldn't buy Bristol Myers Squibb. However, for most investors, including dividend, value, and perhaps even growth-focused types, the stock is probably worth a deep dive. The market doesn't appear to be giving the tech giant enough credit for its success on the development front, and that is probably tilting the risk-reward scale toward reward.

    • The Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans opened up the week on "Thursday Night Football," but quarterback Daniel Jones continued to struggle, completing just 44.4% of pass attempts for 144 yards and a pick.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We are officially halfway done with the 2026 NFL season, and the NFL is now into Week 11, highlighted by the year's final international game: the Minnesota Vikings take on the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, Mexico, for "Sunday Night Football.".

    The Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans opened up the week on "Thursday Night Football," but quarterback Daniel Jones continued to struggle, completing just 44.4% of pass attempts for 144 yards and a pick. The Colts followed up with a statement move on Friday, announcing the team would release Jones and promote former No. 4 overall pick Anthony Richardson Sr. to the starting position in a stunning move.

    Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua might be done for the year after undergoing surgery on his MCL on Tuesday. Nacua was already on injured reserve with multiple injuries, but head coach Sean McVay says that he is now poised to miss "a couple months.".

    That news came one day after Nacua was reportedly suspended three games by the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy, as a result of the receiver's series of incidents this offseason; Nacua is serving the suspension while on IR.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates, and more.

    Recent findings suggest that patriots receiver A.J. Brown is poised to miss significant time: The wideout is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks after suffering a hastring injury last week, per ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss.

    Brown has played in just four games this season after sustaining several separate injuries. He was questionable heading into last Sunday's game with ankle and knee problems, but was able to play before suffering the hamstring injury.

    The Chiefs will likely be without Kenneth Walker III again for their Week 11 game against the Cardinals, head coach Andy Reid remarked Friday.

    Walker reported groin tightness last week, and the team decided to give him a rest and sit out the 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Reid said on Wednesday that the running back was "feeling better," but they did not "want to do something stupid.".

    Through 10 weeks, Walker is fourth in rushing in the NFL with 872 yards and tied for fifth in the league among running backs with seven touchdowns.

    Read more about Walker's injury here.

    Following testing, New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye reportedly suffered a fractured right fibula in Week 10, per ESPN. Maye sustained the injury after taking a sack on the first drive of Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions.

    Maye will not require surgery and there is a small chance he could be back for the Patriots late in the regular season if they are contending for an AFC playoff spot.

    Read more about Maye's injury here.

    In a stunning move, Indianapolis has released starting quarterback Daniel Jones. Head coach Shane Steichen announced the news on Friday, adding that Anthony Richardson will be the team's latest starting QB going forward.

    According to recent reports, after being limited in practice on Thursday, Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck will sit out Friday. Head coach Mike LaFleur said the team will prepare veteran Josh Johnson to start this week against the Chiefs.

    The 40-year-old Johnson made two starts last season with the Commanders. The Cardinals are his 15th NFL season.

    After sitting out practice earlier this week, Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is heading in the right direction to get back on the field on Sunday.

    Mayfield missed Wednesday's practice with injuries to his foot and right thumb, and was limited in practice on Thursday. Though Mayfield's designation for Friday isn't yet available, head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Friday that Mayfield looked good in practice and was trending in the right direction to start.

    Mayfield has been dealing with these injuries, but hasn't missed any time. Tampa Bay had a bye last weekend, giving their quarterback a bit more time to rest.

    The injury woes of Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua just got more severe: On Friday, head coach Sean McVay declared that Nacua had undergone surgery on his MCL on Tuesday, and that he'll be out for "a couple months." Timeline-wise, that might rule the receiver out for the rest of the season.

    Nacua was already on injured reserve with knee and turf toe injuries. He is also serving a three-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy, with the suspension occurring while he's on IR.

    Smith left Sunday's game after injuring his ankle. The quarterback has been limited this this week in practice, but will be a full participant on Friday, head coach Aaron Glenn said.

    Wide receivers Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/hip) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) have been ruled out. DT David Onyemata (abdomen), who had his 21-day practice window opened this week, will remain out.

    As the 49ers practiced against the backdrop of the Rocky Mountains this week, the Vikings tried to bring Mexico City to the Midwest. They erected a massive altitude chamber at their Eagan practice facility that simulates the low-pressure environment found at elevations as high as 12,000 feet.

    Over the past five weeks, Vikings players have subjected themselves to aerobic workouts inside the chamber, using treadmills and stationary bikes to simulate the demands of exercising at altitude. The Vikings hope that altitude training inside their own building reduces the shock factor they experience Sunday night, Tyler Williams, the team's vice president of player health and performance, told reporters in Minnesota on Wednesday.

    In an Instagram post, the two-time Pro Bowl defensive end pledged to come back from his injury stronger than ever and to never again jump up to celebrate a significant play.

    "I honestly can't believe it," Hutchinson wrote in his post. "I've jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me. But even something like this won't hold me back.".

    "Two things I know for sure," he added. "1. I always come back stronger. 2. That's the last time I go airborne.".

    Hutchinson injured his knee on the Lions' first defensive series during their matchup in Munich with the Fresh England Patriots on Sunday.

    According to recent reports, reed played 15 of his 16 NFL seasons in Buffalo and was part of those Bills teams that reached four straight Super Bowls. Over 234 career games, he made 951 receptions for 13,198 yards and 87 touchdowns.

    The two-time All-Pro and seven-time Pro Bowler was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2014.

    Sources indicate that on Thursday, Richardson entered midway through the fourth quarter and missed his first two throws of the night. There was no second series; the Texans ran out the clock. And it almost feels like the Colts are trying to run out the clock on Richardson, Jones, Riley Leonard — all of it.

    Head coach Shane Steichen this week stated he takes "everything into account" when it comes to the quarterbacks. He added: "Obviously, the biggest thing is taking care of the football moving forward.".

    Asked about a potential QB change after Thursday's loss, Steichen mentioned, "we'll evaluate everything.".

    Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua has been suspended for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy, the NFL declared Thursday. ESPN's Adam Schefter was the first to report it.

    Recent findings suggest that nacua's suspension will go into effect immediately, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Dec. 14. The All-Pro wideout is currently on injured reserve with knee and turf toe injuries sustained in Week 9's win over the Washington Commanders, and head coach Sean McVay has mentioned he is expected to miss "significant time." If he were healthy by Dec. 14, he would not miss any additional time because of the suspension.

    Nacua's suspension comes following a roller coaster of an offseason, as he faced a civil lawsuit from a woman over an alleged biting incident and antisemitic comments earlier this year. An attorney representing Nacua denied the woman's claim that he made the antisemitic comment while downplaying the bite mark he left on her.

    The Bengals quarterback will not speak on his normal day as he is dealing with an illness, according to the team. If he's feeling better on Friday, he will meet with reporters. He did appear on the practice field and was seen throwing during the open portion, according to The Athletic's Paul Dehner Jr.

    According to recent reports, the 49ers got a welcome sight on Thursday with wide receiver Mike Evans taking part in practice for the first time in a month. The 33-year-old has not played since Week 6 as he deals with an Achilles injury. San Francisco takes on the Vikings on Sunday night in Week 11.

    According to recent reports, after sitting out Wednesday, the Raiders tight end was back on the field for Thursday's practice. Klint Kubiak stated earlier this week that Bowers is considered day-to-day as he deals with an ankle injury suffered during their Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.

    Parker is remaining on as DC, but Mike Pettine will call plays on the defensive side of the ball.

    Recent findings suggest that "A different perspective [will be] good for us," head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Wednesday. "Play-calling is a very collaborative thing.".

    On Thursday, Parker addressed the change saying it's "not ideal" and did not comment directly when asked about his future in Dallas.

    When asked about his future with the Cowboys, Parkers left more up in the air: "We'll cross that bridge when we come to it.".

    Over four seasons in Denver, Moss has 196 total tackles and 3 interceptions. This season, the 26-year-old has 27 total tackle, 8 pass deflections and 1 interception through eight games.

    Moss was the Broncos' third-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.

    The Ravens have sent Humphrey home from the team facility on Thursday in the fallout from a joke about the city of Baltimore earlier this week, and he will be inactive for Week 11.

    In a recent development, during a segment on his podcast, Humphrey was asked what Baltimore was best at making. He first mentioned "The Star Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer, but then uttered a disparaging line that many have understandably found offensive.

    Recent findings suggest that "What is Baltimore best at making?" Humphrey pondered. "They're best at making criminals.".

    Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield dealing with a foot strain and a thumb problem, did not practice on Wednesday. If Mayfield can't go against the Lions on Sunday, Jalon Daniels will get the call again.

    Geno Smith suffered an ankle injury on Sunday. He was limited during Wednesday's practice and the Jets believe the quarterback can start against the Chargers in Week 11.

    Groin tightness caused Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III to sit out Week 10. That allowed rookie Emmett Johnson to run wild against the Falcons. Walker sat out Wednesday's practice and looks unlikely to play against on Sunday. The team could be eyeing the Thanksgiving Day night game against the Bills for a return.

    It's a drastic shift from the confidence and excitement that surrounded the 34-year-old Parker coming out of training camp, when a highly vocal and schematically multiple group of defenders had Dallas brass wondering whether they could solve multi-year defensive woes.

    According to recent reports, parker has not fixed the Cowboys' defense as the unit ranks third-worst in points allowed per game (28.2) and worst in yards (393.8). But consider that last season's Cowboys ranked worst in points allowed and third-worst in yards a year after the Cowboys ranked second worst in points allowed and bottom-five in yards.

    The issues predate Parker. The fix remains elusive.

    • According to recent reports, investors might be worried about a few things.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:23PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    From the start of 2026 to its peak on Oct. 6, the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%), the measuring stick for how the U.S. equity market is performing, posted a price return of 14%. Since that all-time high, though, the benchmark has fallen about 10% (as of Nov. 19).

    According to recent reports, investors might be worried about a few things. They could be more skeptical about all the artificial intelligence (AI) data center spending that's taking place. Elevated inflation and rising interest rates are stealing the show from a macro perspective. And we're past a midterm election cycle that saw the Democrats take control of Congress, introducing regulatory uncertainty.

    Industry observers note that step back. Even after its recent pullback, the S&P 500 index has risen 229% in 10 years. Here's what a $1,000 investment made in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%) a decade ago could have become today.

    The S&P 500 index climbed at a 12.6% annualized rate over the past decade, before dividends. Including dividends, a $1,000 investment in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF 10 years ago would be worth about $3,953 today. That's a 14.7% annualized total return. Investors almost quadrupled their money.

    Industry observers note that the recent drop is a blip on the substantial-picture radar. Even after sliding since early October, the index is still up slightly in 2026.

    What powered the gains? It's mostly earnings. In December 2016, the S&P 500 traded at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 17. This compares the index's price to the profits analysts expect over the next 12 months. Today, the multiple is around 18, slightly below its 10-year average.

    Based on this metric, the valuation barely moved. Forward earnings per share, meanwhile, jumped from $133 (at the end of 2016) to $416 in early November of this year, a 212% increase. Investors didn't make money by paying higher prices. They built wealth because American businesses became far more profitable.

    One sector stands above the rest. Information technology, measured by the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT -7.00%) delivered an annualized total return of roughly 22.7% in the last decade. AI, cloud computing, and surrounding internet-based secular trends made trillion-dollar market caps a common theme. The tech sector now represents 37% of the S&P 500 index. VOO investors own those winners automatically, for an expense ratio of just 0.03%.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Those gains weren't easy to hold on to. The S&P 500 index fell nearly 20% in late 2018, crashed 34% during the COVID-19 panic, slid 25% in the 2022 bear market, and dropped 19% during the 2025 tariff scare. This year alone has brought two declines of 8% or more. Volatility is just a part of the game.

    Each time the market fell, selling felt like the right move. But each time, the index eventually bounced back and went on to new highs.

    It has been revealed that investors who trade in and out usually pay for it. Morningstar's (MORN -0.30%) latest Mind the Gap study found that the average dollar in U.S. mutual funds and ETFs earned 8.7% per year over the decade ended 2025. The funds themselves returned 9.9%. The difference is due to poorly timed buying and selling.

    Industry observers note that missing a few days hurts, too. According to J.P. Morgan (JPM -3.03%) Asset Management, sitting out the 10 best days over the 20-year period from 2006 through 2025 would have cut an investor's annualized return from 11% to 6.6%, an enormous difference.

    Dollar-cost averaging is the solution. This means investing a set amount on a regular schedule, regardless of price. There's no guessing involved. Adding steadily in this manner to the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF is no doubt one of the simplest ways to build wealth.

    When the market is down, like it is now, hang in there.The best results of the past decade came from holding through every pullback.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Recent findings suggest that the stock market has had a rough few weeks. As of Nov. 20, the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%) had declined by about 10.4% in the prior month, largely driven by investor worries over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade. The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 index has declined almost enough to qualify as a bear market, with a drop of nearly 20% since its Oct. 6 record high.

    Sources indicate that but according to Bloomberg reporting from Nov. 13, Goldman Sachs (GS -6.71%) strategists are bullish on the S&P 500 for next year. Recent research from Goldman suggests that the benchmark S&P index will gain 26% in the next 12 months by November 2027, despite possibly lower earnings growth compared to 2026.Let's look at what this might mean for investors -- and why it's a good sign to keep buying stocks with low-cost index funds like S&P 500 ETFs.

    Goldman strategists predict that the S&P 500 will reach 8,700 points in the next 12 months. On Nov. 20, the index closed at about 6,910, so this would imply a gain of about 26% from that level.

    According to recent reports, that's not an outlandish return to expect for the S&P 500. A 26% gain in 12 months would be an exceptionally strong year, much better than the average. But it's well within the realm of possibility.

    Recent findings suggest that keep in mind that the long-term average annual return for the S&P 500, based on historical data since 1928, is 9.98%. And in the past few years, the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%) has delivered annual returns of about 17.8% in 2025, 25% in 2024, and 26.3% in 2023.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Why does Goldman think the S&P 500 will do so well in the next 12 months? If so many investors are nervous about tech companies spending too much on AI data centers, isn't now a bad time to buy the S&P? After all, as of Nov. 19, eight of the top 10 holdings in the S&P 500 were tech names, and those top eight stocks made up about 33.5% of the index by weight.

    The answer is in the valuations.

    Recent findings suggest that recent investor skepticism about AI stocks might actually be healthy for future returns. Recent declines in tech stock prices have driven down those companies' valuations. Goldman's research finds that AI hyperscalers are trading "well below" their historic valuations and says that "we see Technology -- and Hyperscalers in particular -- as relatively defensive.".

    The very same tech stocks that have been going through a correction in the past month might be poised for bigger gains in the next 12 months. Goldman states that even though some of the biggest hyperscalers have negative cash flow due to their aggressive AI investments, these companies still have strong balance sheets and could become attractive in the next 12 months if growth opportunities elsewhere are harder to find.

    This trend of lower valuations can also be seen if you look at the S&P 500 index forward price-to-earnings ratio (P/E). This metric indicates the index's earnings multiple based on the next 12 months' estimated earnings. The S&P forward P/E has dropped from a recent high of 30 to 21.08, trading at about a 15% discount compared to its five-year average.

    S&P 500 P/E Ratio Forward Estimate data by YCharts.

    Long-term investors need to think beyond today, tomorrow, or even the next 12 months. One year is not "long term." But this Goldman Sachs research is a helpful sign that there are many reasons to be optimistic about the stock market, despite some recent volatility.

    If you share Goldman's optimism about the S&P 500 in 2027, now can be a good time to buy low-cost index funds like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO). This ultra-low-cost ETF lets you track the performance of the S&P.

If Goldman's analysis is on target, your investment in the ETF could go up by 26% in the next 12 months.

    But even if that forecast doesn’t come true, you can rest assured that the S&P 500 has delivered strong average annual returns of about 10% for long-term investors who can buy and hold through temporary ups and downs along the way.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 8:45PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Chipotle Mexican Grill ›.
    • Choosing between Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG -2.07%) and Hershey (HSY +0.82%) depends on whether you value aggressive expansion or reliable brand power.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 8:45PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Chipotle Mexican Grill ›.

    Choosing between Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG -2.07%) and Hershey (HSY +0.82%) depends on whether you value aggressive expansion or reliable brand power.

    Chipotle leads the fast-casual space with its focus on fresh ingredients and digital efficiency. Hershey dominates the confectionery market with a massive portfolio of snacks and sweets. This comparison helps you decide which of these consumer giants better aligns with your financial goals heading into 2027.

    In a recent development, chipotle Mexican Grill focuses on its mission of serving real ingredients across more than 4,000 restaurants in the United States, Canada, Europe, and the Middle East. The firm relies on a robust digital ordering platform that accounts for over 16% of food and beverage revenue, utilizing third-party delivery aggregators to reach more customers. It also expands its global presence through key partnerships, such as the one with Alshaya Group for international restaurant operations.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $12.7 billion, representing growth of approximately 7.9% compared to the prior period. The company reported net income of close to $1.4 billion, which reflects a net margin of approximately 10.8% for the period.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Hershey operates as a dominant force among consumer discretionary stocks through its massive portfolio of chocolate, sweets, and mints. The manufacturer sells its products through wholesale distributors and mass merchandisers, with McLane Company accounting for approximately 27% of consolidated net sales in 2025. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business since the loss of such a large partner could significantly impact overall sales.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 27, 2026, revenue reached close to $12.3 billion, an increase of roughly 6.7% over the previous 12 months. The company achieved net income of approximately $1.8 billion, which contributed to a net margin of nearly 14.6% during this timeframe.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that chipotle Mexican Grill faces significant risks related to food safety and potential food-borne illness incidents, which can severely damage its brand reputation and increase operating costs. The company also deals with intense competition from traditional restaurants and newer entities like ghost kitchens or delivery services such as Starbucks (SBUX -1.28%). Furthermore, the business must navigate legal and regulatory challenges regarding labor practices.

    According to recent reports, hershey is sensitive to the availability and pricing volatility of key raw materials such as cocoa, sugar, and dairy. Supply chain disruptions caused by climate change or natural disasters could negatively impact its manufacturing operations across its global facilities. The organization also faces pressure to successfully implement digital transformation and strategic business realignment programs to stay competitive against other snack manufacturers in a rapidly evolving retail environment.

    Hershey appears cheaper than Chipotle Mexican Grill based on traditional metrics.

    Sources indicate that chipotle is a story about growth and Hershey is about rebounding profitability, and knowing that can help find what the best fit for a portfolio is. For Chipotle, revenue increased 9.6% in the third quarter of 2026 to $3.3 billion. Transactions increased by 0.8%, comparable sales rose 2.1%, and digital sales jumped 38.8%. On top of that, Chipotle opened 84 latest locations and expects to open up to 370 new restaurants by the end of 2026. That mentioned, its operating margin dropped from 15.9% to 13.7%, and earnings per share dipped 6.9% despite the noticeable increase in revenue growth. Overall, while revenue growth and location expansion look impressive, shareholders will want to make sure higher costs aren't cutting too deeply into profitability.

    For Hershey in its third quarter, while revenue increased only 3%, adjusted earnings per share (EPS) rose 103% and net income climbed 112%. Gross margin also increased from 32.6% to 46.1%. That remarked, organic sales increased only 0.8%, while international sales fell 7.5%. What Hershey is seeing appears to be improved results driven by better margins and lower costs, rather than pure consumer demand.

    Between the two, if you prioritize more long-term sales growth potential, Chipotle may be the better fit for a portfolio. For anyone looking for a more mature business model with improving profitability, Hershey may be the better option.

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 20, 2026 at 8:52PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Amazon ›.

    Amazon (AMZN -4.10%) has a significant week ahead. Its cloud computing arm, Amazon Web Services (AWS), hosts its yearly re:Invent conference in Las Vegas from Monday, Nov. 30, to Friday, Dec. 4. AWS calls re:Invent its flagship annual conference, and it's where the unit launches many new products every year.

    It's tempting to think the stock might get a boost when AWS shows off what it's built. To find out, I checked how Amazon shares did in the month after each of the past 10 conferences, from 2016 through 2025, and compared that with the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%).

    Shares trade near $257 as I write, up about 12% this year and well ahead of the S&P 500's rise of about 5%. Amazon now stands about 9% below its Aug. 3 record close of $284.02.

    According to recent reports, not really. For every year, I measured from the close on the trading day before the conference started to the close a month after opening day, using the same window for the S&P 500.

    Industry observers note that amazon stock rose in just four of the 10 windows. It beat the index in four of them, too. And its median return was a drop of around 0.7%, but the S&P 500's median was a gain of about 2.1%.

    The best year was 2024, when Amazon climbed around 6% in the month after the conference while the index dropped about 3%.

    The worst was 2022. Other factors can easily outweigh a week of product news, and that year the stock had already lost about 44% before the conference began. It slid another 12% in the month that followed, compared with a 6% decline in the S&P 500.

    Industry observers note that last year was closer to a wash. After the event ran from Dec. 1 to Dec. 5, 2025, Amazon stock slipped about 1% for the month, while the index was about flat.

    According to recent reports, in short, there's no consistent post-conference rally in the record. Amazon has lagged the S&P 500 more often than not after re:Invent -- in six of those 10 windows.

    Industry observers note that the week of the conference hasn't been much better. Measured from the previous close to that Friday's close, Amazon stock fell during six of those 10 conference weeks.

    The 2024 event makes the strongest case that AWS's news can matter. That year, AWS rolled out its Nova family of artificial intelligence (AI) models and made servers built with its Trainium2 AI chips available to customers. Amazon shares climbed every trading day that week and gained around 9%, while the S&P 500 added about 1%.

    According to recent reports, but last year's lineup was arguably just as major. AWS made servers built with its next-generation Trainium3 chips available and unveiled its Nova 2 models, and the stock dipped about 2% in the conference week.

    What does seem to move Amazon stock is its quarterly reports. Shares surged around 15% on July 31, the day after Amazon released its second-quarter results. In one day, the stock moved more than it did in any of those 10 post-conference months.

    That makes sense, because AWS is where most of Amazon's profit comes from.

    In the third quarter of 2026, AWS posted $17.8 billion in operating income, up 55% year over year. This was around 63% of Amazon's $28.1 billion in total operating income for the period.

    Recent findings suggest that plus AWS's sales growth keeps accelerating. Its revenue rose 39% in the third quarter, faster than the second quarter's 37% and almost twice the 20% growth AWS had a year earlier.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Of course, all this takes heavy spending. Amazon still expects around $220 billion in cash capital expenditures in 2026, and that could weigh on its free cash flow for a while. And the stock isn't cheap, at about 25 times earnings based on what analysts expect for 2027. But with AWS growing almost twice as fast as it was a year ago, I think the price is fair.

    In a recent development, so, is the month after re:Invent a good time to own Amazon stock? Going by the last 10 years, not especially. After all, four weeks is a short window, and I wouldn't use the record as a reason to rush in before the conference or to wait till after it.

    I'd consider buying Amazon shares for the growth AWS keeps posting every quarter. I just wouldn't time my purchase around Nov. 30.

    By Randy Coon – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 9:09PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than CrowdStrike ›.

    Industry observers note that two cybersecurity giants could be joining forces. But would a deal make CrowdStrike a better investment?

    The cybersecurity industry may be on the verge of a blockbuster deal.

    According to reports, CrowdStrike (CRWD -5.76%) is in talks to acquire Zscaler (ZS -5.29%), potentially bringing together two of the industry's most innovative companies in a transaction that could reshape the competitive landscape.

    Investors reacted quickly sending Zscaler shares soaring roughly 17% in after-hours trading, while CrowdStrike shares fell about 8%.

    For long-term investors, the question is what this combination could mean five or ten years from now.

    In a recent development, crowdStrike built its reputation protecting endpoints; the laptops, servers, and devices businesses rely on every day. Its Falcon platform uses artificial intelligence to identify and stop threats.

    Zscaler approaches cybersecurity from another angle, pioneering zero-trust security that helps businesses safely connect employees to applications and data.

    Put them together, and you potentially have something special: a comprehensive security platform protecting devices, owners, networks, and cloud applications.

    This is an incredibly powerful combo because cybersecurity customers increasingly want fewer vendors, simpler solutions, and better protection. And this combo creates an enormous opportunity.

    First, cross-selling. CrowdStrike could introduce Zscaler's capabilities to its existing customers, while Zscaler could do the same with Falcon.

    It has been revealed that second, competitive advantage. A combined company could become a more formidable competitor to Palo Alto Networks (PANW -5.09%) , strengthening its position in an increasingly consolidated industry.

    Third, artificial intelligence. As businesses deploy more AI-powered applications and autonomous agents, protecting their digital infrastructure becomes increasingly complicated and increasingly essential.

    In a recent development, great acquisitions aren't automatically great investments. Zscaler carried a market capitalization of roughly $32 billion before the reports surfaced. That's a substantial price tag, and integrating two large technology platforms isn't easy.

    CrowdStrike would also need to demonstrate that the benefits justify the acquisition premium, financing costs, and potential shareholder dilution.

    Cybersecurity isn't a passing trend. It's becoming essential infrastructure for the digital economy. A CrowdStrike-Zscaler combination could create a powerhouse positioned to benefit from that transformation for years. But remember: A great business isn't always a great stock at any price.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) just wrapped up one of its worst weeks in history, falling 8.6% as the AI trade collapsed.
    • According to recent reports, corrections are fairly routine events on the stock market.
    • Nervousness around the AI sector has been pushing tech stocks lower since the beginning of October, but the negative sentiment didn't really hit the S&P 500 until this week.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jeremy Bowman – Nov 20, 2026 at 10:38PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    The S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) just wrapped up one of its worst weeks in history, falling 8.6% as the AI trade collapsed. The index gave up 3.7% on Friday to close in correction territory, defined as a decline of 10% or more from a recent closing high. It was the first time the index had fallen below 7,000 since April.

    According to recent reports, corrections are fairly routine events on the stock market. On average, the S&P 500 enters a correction about every 1.5 years, and its last correction came in March-April of 2025 as concerns about President Trump's tariffs and a trade war drove investors to sell.

    Nervousness around the AI sector has been pushing tech stocks lower since the beginning of October, but the negative sentiment didn't really hit the S&P 500 until this week.

    Investors are worried about rising interest rates squeezing the AI infrastructure build-out, including in the unprofitable neocloud sector; the backlash against data centers following the midterm elections; and the crisis unfolding at Nvidia after Jensen Huang resigned, with investigations into chip exports to China and now an accounting investigation by the SEC.

    Fears of an AI bubble have been swirling in the market for a while, but despite some of the air coming out of these stocks, the fundamentals still look strong and valuations remain cheap.

    Industry observers note that of the last 10 corrections in the S&P 500, which go back to 2011, the average decline has been 17%, and two of those turned into bear markets. That happened during the COVID crash early in 2020 and in 2022, a bear market that lasted most of the year.

    The average duration from peak to a upcoming peak was 9.4 months, and the average duration from the bottom to a new peak was 6.1 months, though the last two corrections took less than 100 days.

    Regardless of the length of time, the S&P 500 has recovered from every correction it's experienced.

    A correction is no reason to panic, and it's a regular part of stock market volatility. However, this is a good time to put together a watch list of stocks you'd like to buy if you have cash available. If you are a net buyer of stocks, a sell-off is actually a good thing, as Warren Buffett advised, as it makes stocks cheaper to buy.

    Some quality stocks like Alphabet and Meta now have price-to-earnings ratios below 20, making them look attractive, and we're likely to see more deals if stocks fall further.

    It has been revealed that if you're not in a position to buy stocks, it's worth remembering that historically, the S&P 500 returns to an all-time high within nine months on average. How this sell-off plays out will depend on the AI sector, but the low valuations for many of the top AI stocks are an encouraging sign.

    #27915. Latest Update: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1021 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1021 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    In a recent development, spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    The high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," remarked Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone remarked.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That said, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, said Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    In a recent development, "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she stated.

    The lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, noted Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he stated. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    Industry observers note that in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

    "It is isolated," she remarked. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    It has been revealed that but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin noted. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    Sources indicate that it's also notable to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, mentioned R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo stated.

    "That's when spreads really widen out," he remarked. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) finished at 23,879 on Thursday, Nov.
    • The standard line for a bear market is a 20% fall from the high.
    • Industry observers note that I'm not predicting the index gets there.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 20, 2026 at 10:57PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Alphabet ›.

    The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) finished at 23,879 on Thursday, Nov. 19. The tech-heavy index now sits about 13.5% below its Oct. 6 record close of 27,600 -- a correction, though not a bear market.

    The standard line for a bear market is a 20% fall from the high. For the Nasdaq, that's a close near 22,080, or about another 7.5% drop from Thursday's level.

    Industry observers note that I'm not predicting the index gets there. But a plan is easier to stick to when it's written down before a sell-off than during one, and mine is this: If the Nasdaq closes in bear-market territory, the first stock I'll buy is Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%)(GOOG -2.59%).

    Industry observers note that shares of the Google parent closed at $272.66 on Thursday, their lowest close since October 2025. The stock's now about 32% below where it finished the day on May 13, at a record close of $402.62 -- more than double the Nasdaq's decline from its own high.

    A lot of that drop came in a single session. The stock fell about 13% on Oct. 29, the day after Alphabet posted third-quarter results showing slower Search growth, lower earnings per share, and a second straight quarter of negative free cash flow.

    In other words, the stock's arguably already taken the sort of hit a bear market brings, while the business underneath keeps growing.

    Showing how well the business has held up through the drop, Alphabet's revenue growth has accelerated all year. Sales grew 22% year over year in the first quarter, then 24% in the second, and third-quarter sales rose 25% to $127.6 billion. Operating income grew 30% year over year in all three quarters. And in the first nine months of 2026, operating income came to $121 billion, a 30% jump from $93 billion a year before.

    I focus on operating income because Alphabet's net income swings with the value of its stakes in other companies. Other income (mainly investment gains) added around $127 billion in the same nine months.

    It has been revealed that that mentioned, not every number is heading the right way. Last year's third quarter had a $3.5 billion European Commission fine, so without it, operating income rose more like 17% in the latest quarter. And as spending on artificial intelligence (AI) reveals up in costs, the operating margin has shrunk. It was 31.8% in the third quarter, versus 34% in the April-to-June period and 36.1% in the first quarter.

    The second reason is the balance sheet. Alphabet expects to spend between $195 billion and $205 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, and management mentioned that amount is expected to rise significantly in 2027. A bear market could make raising money for that sort of spending more expensive.

    But Alphabet has already raised a lot of it. In the first nine months of 2026, the company raised about $85 billion in new debt, about $43 billion by selling common stock, and another $19 billion by issuing preferred stock.

    Alphabet's cash and marketable securities totaled $265.1 billion at the end of September, more than twice its total at the end of 2025. Long-term debt was $125.1 billion.

    Yes, selling new shares dilutes current shareholders, and free cash flow was negative in both of the past two quarters. But with around $140 billion more in cash and marketable securities than in long-term debt, Alphabet arguably doesn't need a steady stock market to keep funding its build-out.

    It has been revealed that alphabet stock doesn't look expensive to me now. At $272.66, it costs around 18 times expected 2027 earnings, while Meta Platforms, another ad-driven tech giant, trades at about 17 times its expected 2027 earnings. For a business growing operating income by double digits, I think the price is fair.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that I wouldn't argue with anyone buying some now. The reason to wait for the line is that a bear market would probably mark down many stocks at once. Deciding beforehand which one gets the first dollar stops me from chasing whatever happened to fall the most that week.

    Sources indicate that alphabet doesn't have to track the index, either. But if it just matched the Nasdaq's remaining 7.5% drop from Thursday's close, the stock would trade near $252, or about 17 times expected 2027 earnings.

    If the Nasdaq closes 20% below its record, Alphabet is likely where my blueprint begins.

    Industry observers note that sure, the index might never get there. And if it doesn't, Alphabet at around 18 times expected 2027 earnings still looks fairly priced to me.

    • Recent findings suggest that dan Loeb is widely considered one of the world's top investors, starting his Third Point hedge fund with a few million dollars in 1995 and turning it into an over-$28 billion behemoth.
